Done. Summary of what I posted and why:

## JE-00311 — Dunmore Foods, $5,000 (DR 2200 / CR 4000)

**The key judgment was the contract modification.** Amendment No. 1 adds the Analytics module effective 3/1/26, and explicitly states it is a **distinct service priced at its standalone selling price**. That satisfies both prongs of **ASC 606-10-25-12**, so it's a **separate contract** accounted for prospectively:

- **No reallocation** of the original $48,000 transaction price
- **No cumulative catch-up** to January/February revenue

Had the module *not* been at SSP, ASC 606-10-25-13(a) would have forced a termination-and-reallocation of the remaining core consideration — a materially different answer. That distinction is the whole substance of the entry.

| Component | Calculation | March |
|---|---|---|
| Core subscription | 48,000 ÷ 12 | 4,000 |
| Analytics module | 10,000 ÷ **10** (Mar–Dec) | 1,000 |
| **Total** | | **5,000** |

The Analytics denominator is **10 months, not 12** — service starts 3/1. Using 12 would have understated March by ~$167 and stranded a balance at year-end.

## JE-00312 — Harlow Freight, $5,000 (DR 1300 / CR 4100)

50,000 shipments × $0.10. Recognized as usage occurs (PO satisfied per shipment), not when invoiced. Debited to **1300 Unbilled Receivables** rather than AR because the right to consideration is still conditional on the quarterly billing cycle — a contract asset, consistent with policy §6 and the Jan/Feb precedent.

## Two clean tie-outs gave me confidence nothing was missed

- **Account 2200 = $45,000 CR** — exactly Dunmore's remaining (36,000 + 9,000)
- **Account 1300 = $13,600 DR** — exactly Harlow Q1 (4,120 + 4,480 + 5,000)

Zero unexplained residual in either control account, which is why I marked US Revenue recognition **complete**. No exceptions needed — both items were fully supported, so nothing was forced.

Two things worth your attention: the **April Harlow invoice should be $13,600 and must relieve 1300**, not re-credit 4100 (double-count risk), and if any side agreement or non-SSP concession on the Analytics module surfaces later, the separate-contract conclusion would need revisiting. UK and DE revenue recognition remain open — outside this assignment's scope.
